draft.title: AI-based visual quality inspection integrated with the ERP on two stamping lines at Kowadło Precyzja
draft.summary: Kowadło Precyzja Sp. z o.o. plans to roll out AI-based visual quality inspection on two lines stamping steel parts for household appliance makers and to connect it to its ERP system. The goal is to replace manual spot checks and to report rejects and defect causes automatically.

sections.heading: Problem and current situation
sections.body:
The company (about 45 people, two shifts) stamps steel parts for household appliance makers. Quality control is manual and based on spot checks, and the number of complaints is rising. Information about rejects and defect causes does not reach the ERP reports automatically.

[To complete: number of complaints and cost of defects over the last 12 months — baseline values for the indicators.]

sections.heading: Solution and project scope
sections.body:
1. Requirements analysis: defect types to detect, line cycle time, camera mounting points.
2. Supply and installation of vision stations on two stamping lines.
3. Preparation and validation of an AI model that recognises defects in part images.
4. ERP integration: rejects and defect causes recorded automatically.
5. Training for operators and the quality team — as an additional cost, within the 40% limit of eligible costs.

The project may not start before the application is submitted. [To complete: contractors selected on the basis of at least 3 quotes.]

sections.heading: Results and indicators
sections.body:
Every part on both lines inspected instead of spot checks; rejects and defect causes recorded in the ERP without manual re-entry; fewer quality complaints.

[To complete with baseline and target values: number of complaints, share of defects caught before shipment, time from detecting a defect to the report.]

sections.heading: Budget and schedule
sections.body:
Dig.IT 2/2026: grant of PLN 150–850k, up to 50% of eligible costs, de minimis aid, reimbursed after the project ends — the company pre-finances the full cost until settlement. The grant may not exceed 30% of average annual net revenue over the last 3 years.

[To complete: budget from the quotes, own contribution, schedule of stages 1–5.]
